responsiveness_rationale: Both halves of the question are answered by rows rather than by inference. The named subsection is returned as its own record and named again as the subject of several observations, and those observations place the deep microseismicity beneath that subsection's ridge axis, give its depth band twice over from two different blocks, deny any events below the lower edge of that band, and put the shallow off-axis seismicity to the west of the same axis. The earthquake population is present as depth-bounded observations rather than as a catalogue object, which is enough to answer where the events sit. Two caveats worth recording and neither of them fatal: the spatial relation is carried in the free-text quantity descriptions of subject-bound observations, not as a typed relation between the subsection and an event population, and none of the seven returned relations connects the two; and a minority of rows attach general ridge-class expectations and location-error statistics to features the cited blocks never name, which is noise around an otherwise direct answer. Several supporting rows also derive from figure-caption blocks, which the question's own scope excludes as an answer surface.
